payload.name: Preserve concrete event details
payload.description: When extracting or updating event/relationship memories and the source message names concrete details (participants, actors, reasons, quotes, descriptors, topics, request specifics) that could be paraphrased away, retrieve this skill.
content: When extracting event/relationship memories, preserve all explicitly stated concrete specifics verbatim: participants, subject's role, actors, reasons/topics, co-participants (including 'we' and named companions), and enumerated items; do not generalize them away.
Preserve direct quotes and exact evaluative descriptors verbatim (e.g., 'not too serious', a promise's exact wording) instead of paraphrasing; such text is often queried by exact wording.

Before SKIPping a candidate as duplicate or during MERGE/UPDATE, verify the existing memory contains every specific detail (each enumerated topic, association, old fact) and preserve original event dates; if missing, MERGE/ADD.
For explicit help requests, record who asked, who was asked, and the exact topic/task as an event; do not collapse to a general statement of need.

Before SKIPping for duplication/coverage, locate a concrete existing memory version in the current snapshot or committed history that contains the same subject–predicate–object fact (and compatible time bounds); earlier candidates, conversation context, or assumptions do not count as evidence.
If no covering memory exists — including an empty snapshot or null target_memory_id — do not SKIP; ADD the candidate (or MERGE/UPDATE into the closest partially covering memory) so the fact persists.

If only part of the candidate overlaps existing content, preserve every non-overlapping fact (e.g., emotional state, distinct project, named detail) via ADD/MERGE; never skip the whole candidate for partial coverage.
Treat 'overlap' as the same specific fact/project/event, not merely same domain or subject; distinct items (book vs screenplay, camping vs hiking) require their own memory even if topically related.

Preserve exact artifact/object names and scope qualifiers (e.g., 'a few bits for a screenplay', 'the first act', 'hoodies') instead of broadening; keep quantity/ordinal wording and running totals for series.
Keep intensity/frequency/duration modifiers (nonstop, constantly, every day, for hours) verbatim; do not soften them.
Resolve relative time expressions (yesterday, last week) to concrete world dates before storing event start.
Resolve every pronoun to the entity active in surrounding context; prefer the current topic, not the first or last mentioned.
If ambiguity remains, do not guess a wrong subject; preserve the fact without a subject rather than misattributing.

payload.name: Preserve dialogue relationship and attribution facts
payload.description: When a message includes direct address (nicknames), disclosures to named people, second-person statements about the addressee's condition, or explicit identity claims (e.g., 'pets are family'), retrieve this skill during extraction.
content: When a message directly addresses a named person, preserve the vocative form as a relationship fact (speaker uses this nickname/name for addressee), separate from any main event.
When one participant discloses a personal event to a named addressee (e.g., 'Hey Sam, I got married'), record that the speaker informed that addressee, not just the event.

When a reply concerns the addressee's own condition (health, injury, etc.), attribute the state/event to the addressee, not the speaker; preserve any reported assessment (e.g., doctor's comment) verbatim.
When a message states an explicit identity/relationship belief (e.g., 'pets are family'), create a profile/relationship memory even if event details exist.

When a message describes attributes, preferences, or reactions of an entity other than the speaker (e.g., pets, family, friends), set the memory subject to that entity and preserve the specific fact (e.g., 'my dogs hate snow' → subject = dogs).
Extract owned entities' specific reactions to conditions as distinct facts, separate from ownership/general preferences.
Verify pronoun agreement and preserve the speaker's relationship in the content (e.g., 'Audrey's dogs').

When a message explicitly states an intent to tell, inform, announce, or share news with a specific person or group (e.g., 'telling my work friends', 'I've been meaning to tell you'), extract the sharer, audience, and exact news content as worded, and create a separate candidate for the intent even if the underlying fact is also extracted, so queries about wanting to share remain answerable. Do not apply to plain facts without sharing wording, or when the same intent with the same audience is already stored; skip inferring implicit audience or content.

payload.name: Preserve explicit emotions and their triggers
payload.description: When a message explicitly names emotions or emotional reactions tied to an event, trigger, or relationship, preserve each stated emotion and its cause in the extracted memory.
content: Scan for explicit emotion words (thrilled, discouraged, relief, worry, love) and identify each emotion, its subject, and its trigger; retain every named emotion, including contrasting ones. Also capture explicitly stated personal-state facts such as difficulties, stress sources, motivations, coping links, and response actions, preserving exact wording and any stated trigger/object.
Extract emotional assessments as separate state/event candidates alongside factual events or plans; do not let a plan-only candidate replace or omit the affect.
Before SKIP/merge of a candidate, verify whether any stated feeling is already stored; if not, ADD a new memory or UPDATE/MERGE a related memory to include it.
When a message narrates a challenge and states response actions, extract the response actions as a separate candidate with the problem link and temporal markers as stated.

Do not infer personal states from tone, context, or absence; apply only when the message explicitly names the feeling, difficulty, source, driver, function, or response action. Skip conventional greetings/closings.

When a message mixes emotional/evaluative language with an explicit factual claim (specific date, year, relationship, or event occurrence), extract the factual claim as its own memory (event, profile, or relationship) in addition to any emotional memory. Preserve the exact date, year, relationship, and participants as stated; do not paraphrase, generalize, or replace them with emotional context. Do not apply this to messages that contain only emotional/evaluative language without an explicit factual claim; do not infer or complete dates, relationships, or events that are not explicitly stated.

payload.name: Preserve specific evaluative descriptors and couplings
payload.description: When a message attaches an explicit evaluation, descriptor, or feeling to a specific entity, activity, place, work, or process, keep that exact wording and pairing in the extracted candidate.
content: Identify explicit evaluative phrases about an entity, event, or activity (e.g., 'looks amazing', 'atmosphere was electric', 'blew my mind') and preserve them verbatim or closely.
Keep the specific referent paired with the feeling or assessment (e.g., '<place> gives me peace', '<activity> felt freeing'); do not replace these with a generic summary of the event.
Preserve every distinct claim from the source, objective and subjective; do not collapse the message into one headline or a vague sentiment like 'enjoyed it'.
For creative works, also preserve the creator's process description (e.g., 'with a sense of joy and freedom', 'without restraint') alongside the emotional content.

When a message states an activity and its explicit purpose, benefit, origin, or intended impact (e.g., 'to keep me busy', 'a great escape', 'got me into it'), preserve that rationale verbatim alongside the activity and emit it as its own preference or state fact (e.g., '<subject> values <reason>'). Also detect explicit phrases of personal significance: 'reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'is so beautiful', 'I love', 'helps me stay focused', 'brings me joy', 'to remind me to'. Capture the object/attribute, the stated meaning/feeling/commitment, and the speaker; preserve the exact verb (e.g., 'misses', 'reminds') in the stored text. Classify memory: relationship if pointing to people, preference for likes/aesthetics, state for functional benefit, value/commitment for 'reminds me to'. Do not skip because the statement is casual, object-centric, or unrequested; if a profile exists, update/merge instead of duplicating.

When a message explicitly states why, how, or for what purpose someone started, does, or learned an activity, or what inspires their work, preserve that stated context verbatim with the activity (e.g., 'my friend got me into it', 'I started because...', 'it's my escape', 'I was inspired by...', 'I taught myself'). Do not let the context be subsumed into a generic 'likes/enjoys' summary.
When answering a direct question (e.g., 'how did you get into X?', 'what inspired you?', 'what is it for?'), treat the reply as an explicit fact even if short.
Never infer or invent purposes, origins, motivations, sources, or learning methods that are not stated; skip if the statement is absent or already recorded.

payload.name: Extract embedded subjective self-reports
payload.description: When a brief, casual, exclamatory, or narrative message includes a first-person self-report of feelings, stress, coping, or comfort about an activity, extract it as a state or preference memory even without structured event/plan details.
content: Scan every message for explicit first-person evaluations like 'it feels magical', 'dealing with work stress', or 'photos give me peace'; do not skip because it is short, encouraging, or story-like.
Extract the exact subject, feeling/effect, and cause/activity as a state or preference candidate; for comfort/cheer statements also create a separate positive-fact memory.
Include time qualifiers if present (e.g., 'this week'); otherwise treat as current or durable according to the wording.
If a memory for the activity already exists, UPDATE/MERGE with the new feeling rather than dropping the fact or creating a duplicate.

payload.name: Extract named hobbies of mentioned people
payload.description: When a message names a hobby, interest, or passion of another person (e.g., 'was one of her hobbies'), preserve each concrete activity as a profile/preference memory for that person.
content: For every explicitly named activity or interest of a mentioned person, create or update a profile/preference memory for that person, even if the message is emotional or about grief.
List each distinct hobby separately; do not let one emotional or event candidate subsume multiple concrete facts.
Preserve exact activity names rather than paraphrasing to a general 'hobbies' or 'interests' label.

payload.name: Extract interpersonal advice as memory candidates
payload.description: When a message contains one participant advising, suggesting, or recommending a course of action to another (e.g., 'you should...', 'try...', 'maybe look into...'), during extraction create a candidate preserving the advice.
content: Create one candidate per advisory utterance recording advisor, addressee, exact recommended action, and stated purpose; include hedged or tentative wording.
If the advice prompted a plan or commitment in a later message, include the originating suggestion message so attribution and full advised topics are preserved.
Do not skip because the phrasing is imperative, casual, or not a factual statement; do not require later confirmation or a state change.

Detect explicit offers of help, tips, advice, or ongoing support (e.g., 'let me know if you need', 'I can give you', 'happy to help with') and capture speaker (provider), recipient, offered thing, and topic; note the future/availability nature.
Do not skip such offers even if mixed with chit-chat or closing remarks; submit to CRUD for ADD/UPDATE.
During CRUD, add the suggestion as a distinct event/state with speaker and addressee fields; do NOT merge it into the addressee's preference/plan unless the addressee later explicitly affirms it.

payload.name: Extract explicit self-disclosed preferences separately
payload.description: When a message contains an explicit first-person statement of liking, loving, preferring, or a favorite (e.g., 'I love...', 'my favorite is...'), during extraction create a preference candidate for each named item.
content: Scan every message for explicit preference signals such as 'favorite', 'love', 'like', 'prefer', 'enjoy', or 'one of my favorites'; create a preference candidate when present.
Record each distinct liked item in its own candidate, preserving exact item name and all modifiers (e.g., 'dairy-free chocolate mousse'), plus relational context like 'besides X' if stated.
If the same turn also contains an event such as recommending or sharing, emit both a preference memory and an event memory; do not let the event subsume the preference.

payload.name: Preserve recommendation acts with recipients
payload.description: When a message shows a speaker recommending specific items to a named recipient (e.g., 'I recommend X to Y', 'you should play Z'), during extraction and CRUD keep the directional recommendation act, not just a preference statement.
content: Extract the recommendation as an event or relationship naming recommender, recipient, and item list; include this explicitly in memory content (e.g., 'A recommended X, Y, Z to B').
When updating existing memories, do not overwrite the recommendation framing with an enjoyment-only summary; preserve prior facts and add the recommendation clause.
After drafting, verify every explicit recommendation retains its source and target direction; if missing, revise before committing.

If a recommendation/advice message directly follows a turn in which exactly one other participant asked for a recommendation (e.g., 'Any suggestions?'), record that participant as the recipient (e.g., 'John recommended Barcelona to Tim'), even if the reply says only 'you'.
When the recipient is ambiguous (multiple people asked, or message is group-directed), do NOT guess; skip the recipient field rather than assigning one.
Preserve the message timestamp (or explicit date) as the date of the recommendation speech act; do not invent a date.

During CRUD, if a recommendation event's date differs from an existing memory it would merge into, keep the new date (or keep separate) so 'When did X recommend Y to Z?' remains answerable; do not overwrite the newer date.

payload.name: Extract explicit standing facts and precise claims
payload.description: When a message contains an explicit standing preference, ability, progress observation, or a specific situation-bound claim (e.g., 'I love competing', 'hard work is paying off', 'could write a movie in cool places'), during extraction.
content: When a message reports an event but also explicitly states a standing preference/ability, extract that preference as its own memory, not just the event; during CRUD, add it separately rather than overwriting the event.
When one person observes another's progress, achievement, or milestone, extract a state/event memory with speaker attribution; separate the concrete milestone from the evaluative praise.
When a speaker states a specific capability/feeling tied to a situation or place, preserve the exact action and context verbatim instead of absorbing it into a generic trait.
When a message states how media or an experience changed the speaker's view or inspired them, keep the user's exact phrasing and concepts rather than paraphrasing to 'motivated him'.

When a speaker names a specific media title and states a reaction, evaluation, recency/first-experience timing, or intent to consume (e.g., 'recently watched', 'can't wait to see'), extract an event/plan memory preserving exact title, speaker, stated verb, timing, and reaction. For relative first-experience timing, anchor to message timestamp and preserve wording; do not invent a date and do not apply without a specific title or stated trigger. If a separate durable preference/reason is stated, create a separate preference; do not merge event/plan into preference.

payload.name: Extract events from contextual self-reports
payload.description: When a message mentions a project completion with a timing cue, or pairs a life-event noun with an explicit date while focusing on something else, retrieve this skill during extraction.
content: Scan each message for completion verbs (finished, completed, submitted) used by the speaker about their own work; if a timing cue is present (last week, yesterday, date), create an event candidate capturing the work phrase and the time.

Also scan for life-event nouns (wedding, trip, graduation, birthday) paired with an explicit year/date even when the message is about photos or reminiscing; extract a dated event candidate with participants.
Do not require a full date or a named project; a descriptive noun phrase plus relative time is enough. Do not infer events not explicitly stated.

payload.name: Preserve event facts and dates on updates
payload.description: When a CRUD UPDATE/MERGE or enrichment would rewrite an existing event/state memory with later evidence — re-description, new date, or separate occurrence — retrieve this to keep original facts, timestamps, and distinct events intact.
content: Before overwriting, compare event identity (world_start, ordinal, participants, target/action). If it's a distinct occurrence, ADD a new memory and leave the original unchanged; only UPDATE the same real-world event with compatible refinements.

Keep prior world_start/world_end unless the new message explicitly re-dates the same event. Preserve precise dates and event verbs (joined, started, moved); don't convert a dated one-time event into a timeless state or let a later follow-up shift the timestamp.

Retain all previously stored specific facts, concrete details, and durable preferences/goals. Don't replace a precise earlier record with a vaguer paraphrase. Classify stated desires as preference/plan; if a new event threatens one, keep it in the updated content or a separate ADD.
During extraction, resolve relative time phrases ('last week', 'yesterday') to absolute dates from occurred_at and store them in world_start/world_end and content.
Before committing an UPDATE/MERGE, diff the proposed content against the current version; keep every non-contradicted fact verbatim and append new facts rather than replacing the memory wholesale.

If the new facts concern a different topic/object than the stored memory, ADD a separate memory (choose a fitting memory kind) rather than overwriting; only UPDATE when the facts refine the same stored core fact.

Treat distinct preferences, aspects, or events of the same subject as separate memories; preserve exact names, dates, and wording. Do not apply when the message explicitly changes, retracts, or supersedes a stored fact.

When a message explicitly states a current location ('I'm in X') or an activity-location pair ('yoga in the park'), extract it as a state/preference memory with attribute 'current location' or the activity name, value exact wording, and world_start = message date; preserve prepositional phrases verbatim (e.g., 'by a tranquil spot' vs 'at a nearby spot'). Do not let surrounding event or emotional content subsume the location; if ambiguous about who was there or whether it's current, preserve original wording and do not guess.

payload.name: Resume activity updates for stale state memories
payload.description: When a message describes someone performing an activity and an existing preference/state memory says they used to do it but haven't had the chance recently, update that memory with the resumption.
content: While extracting an activity mention, scan preference/state memories for the same subject and activity.
If a stale memory says 'used to ... but no chance recently', create an UPDATE adding the resumption fact with the current occurrence date, not just a standalone event.
During CRUD, prioritize updating the stale memory so the resumed activity remains linked to the earlier preference.

payload.name: Preserve explicit longing and absence statements
payload.description: When a user explicitly states they miss, want, wish for, long for, or lack something, preserve the state verb verbatim as the core claim of a preference/state memory, even with surrounding context.
content: Identify explicit longing/absence phrases: 'miss', 'wish', 'long for', 'want', 'can't do', 'haven't been able to'.
Extract the subject and object, and record the state verb exactly (e.g., 'Andrew misses being in nature while working in the city').
Do not paraphrase longing into softer preferences; review stored text to ensure a future question 'what does the user miss?' can be answered directly.

payload.name: ExtractExplicitStateAndOwnership
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states an entity's current status/condition or that they started/own a business, treat it as a state-memory candidate even if brief or part of small talk.
content: Extract explicit current-status assertions (e.g., 'the store's doing great', 'she's very sick') as state candidates with entity, attribute, value, and timestamp; create the entity if absent.
Do not skip brief, casual, or small-talk status claims — direct self-reports of condition are high-value state memories.

When a message explicitly states a person started/owns their business (e.g., 'my store', 'started my own'), preserve that fact even if another activity is described; if an existing memory covers the activity but not the ownership, enrich it with the missing fact.
Only apply to clear, factual assertions; skip jokes, hypotheticals, and inferred ownership from vague business mentions.

payload.name: Preserve health event context
payload.description: When extracting event memories, if a user message narrates a health scare, medical visit, hospital stay, or check-up outcome, preserve the specific triggering context along with the resolution.
content: When extracting a health/medical event from a user message, capture both the triggering context (e.g., 'during a medical check-up', 'at the ER', 'after a test') and the resolution (e.g., 'turned out to be a misunderstanding'). Do not reduce the event to only hospitalization or final verdict.

If the message separates trigger from outcome, include both clauses in the candidate content to keep the full sequence (e.g., 'found something suspicious during a check-up, which turned out to be a misunderstanding').
For health event memories, preserve the precise setting over the emotional reaction, because the setting distinguishes multiple health events for the same person.

payload.name: Extract reason from reschedule/cancellation
payload.description: When a message cancels or reschedules a meeting/event and includes an explanatory reason such as 'I already have plans' or 'I'm busy', retrieve and extract that reason as a separate fact.
content: When a user message cancels/reschedules a meeting and gives a reason (e.g., 'I already have plans', 'I have a conflict'), extract a candidate for that underlying fact as a state/event, not just the cancellation action.
Capture the person with the plan (usually the speaker), the date/time referenced, and the nature of the plan if disclosed. Do not transfer the plan to the other participant.
If a new meeting time is proposed, create a separate candidate for the rescheduled event; keep the reason as its own candidate to preserve the cause.

payload.name: Extract per-member attributes for enumerated groups
payload.description: When a user describes an enumerated group (e.g., 'the oldest', 'the second', 'the youngest' of pets) assigning a separate trait to each member, retrieve this skill.
content: Detect enumerated-group statements: messages listing two or more members of the same category, each with its own attribute (personality, behavior, preference).
Generate a separate extraction candidate per member, capturing (1) the member identifier (ordinal like 'oldest'/'second', or name) and (2) that member's stated attribute(s).
Do not merge members into one memory or skip informal/subjective traits; preserve exact wording.
Include the ordinal/order in the memory so future queries about 'the oldest', 'the second', etc., can be answered.

payload.name: Preserve media completion status
payload.description: When a person's statement indicates reading, watching, or finishing media, preserve the completion aspect (finished vs ongoing) in stored memory.
content: Record exact completion status from verb tense: perfect/progressive-perfect ('I've been reading', 'I have read', 'I finished') → store as completed/read; present-continuous ('I am reading', 'I'm watching') → store as ongoing.
For ambiguous statements, prefer completed status by default so retrospective questions ('What has X read?') succeed.
Always include the specific title/series/description in the event text.

payload.name: ExtractFrequencyFromConversationalResponse
payload.description: When a message is a reply to a question asking about frequency ('how often', 'how many times', 'every day?') and contains explicit frequency wording ('multiple times a day', 'very often', 'every morning', 'twice a week'), extract a state/preference memory capturing the activity and its frequency.
content: If the current message answers a frequency question (e.g., 'How often...?', 'How many times...?'), identify the activity and the frequency expression in the reply.
Do not skip extraction because the wording is informal or includes intensifiers ('very often', 'even'). Treat explicit frequency phrases as factual evidence.
Create a candidate state (or update an existing one) that records the subject, the activity, and the frequency. Preserve the exact frequency wording when possible.

If the activity and subject are implied by the question and the reply confirms them, use the question context to complete the candidate (e.g., question 'walk dogs' + reply 'multiple times a day' → 'Audrey walks her dogs multiple times a day').

payload.name: Resolve relative times from message timestamps
payload.description: When a message uses a relative time phrase ('yesterday', 'last week', 'next month') for an event/plan and has an occurred_at timestamp, resolve it to a concrete date/range and preserve the original wording.
content: Resolve explicit relative time phrases ('yesterday', 'last week', 'next month') against the message's occurred_at timestamp for world_start/world_end, using the full implied calendar period; never use message, processing, or borrowed dates.
Preserve the speaker's original relative wording in memory content alongside the resolved date/range (e.g., 'last month (December 2023)'); do not replace with vague terms or drop the phrase.

Only resolve when the expression is explicit and a reliable timestamp exists; for vague terms ('recently', 'soon') or missing timestamps, keep wording verbatim, leave dates unset, and do not guess or borrow dates. Never invent or infer a date the speaker did not state; if no anchor or ambiguous, keep only the original wording.
Skip frequency phrases ('every week') and preference/profile statements; during CRUD, correct existing memories whose world_start wrongly equals the message date to the resolved date.

payload.name: Track cumulative counts for repeated events
payload.description: When a message reports another occurrence of the same event type or plan for the same participants (using 'again', 'another', 'second/fourth time'), retrieve to maintain a cumulative-count state memory.
content: During extraction, when a repetition marker ('another', 'again', 'second/third/fourth time') appears for an event type, scan existing event memories for a prior same-type occurrence for the same subject. Do not apply to first-time mentions or refinements of a single plan.

Emit or UPDATE a state memory with the cumulative count equal to the number of distinct recorded occurrences, including the current one (e.g., first + another = 2). Copy exact wording and dates of each occurrence into the event memories; keep each occurrence as its own memory.

For recurring joint plans (even without explicit repetition words), extract each separately agreed instance as a distinct plan and store the aggregate count only from those distinct instances. Skip counting when the message merely re-references/reschedules one existing plan; never infer counts the messages do not support.

payload.name: Preserve transfer/origin events with attribution
payload.description: When a message explicitly states that someone gave, sent, wrote, received, or provided an item to someone (including nostalgic asides and origin stories), preserve the transfer/origin event with the exact action verb, provider, recipient, item, and any stated time/place; include entailed co-presence.
content: When a message contains an explicit transfer verb (gave, sent, wrote, received, handed, provided) naming an item and a sender/recipient, create an event candidate recording the item, sender, recipient, verb, and any stated time/place. If a later message identifies the sender or purpose, update the same event. Do not apply to mere mentions without a transfer verb.

For gift/origin statements with a stated age/time and giver/recipient (e.g., 'when I was 10, my parents got me that'), extract the recipient, giver, exact object, and age/time as a separate event; do not let a hobby/preference candidate subsume it. Resolve pronouns only if unambiguous.

Preserve the exact action verb and provider; do not paraphrase into a passive or agentless form, and never infer gift status, occasion, or unstated details. Do not apply when the provider cannot be confidently resolved.

When the transfer entails both parties being physically together at a stated location/time, record that co-presence (e.g., 'given in Paris' → both were in Paris) without inventing journey details. Also capture items provided for event attendees as a provision detail when stated.

Detect implicit sharing cues (e.g., 'here's a pic', 'look at X', 'I made you a card', 'this is my collection', 'just look at my to-do list!') and create an event candidate with sharer, recipient/time if stated, and the exact item named. Include stated origin, subject, or inspiration in the same candidate using exact wording; never invent content, depiction, or participants. Keep the sharing event separate from preference, hobby, or state candidates; do not let one subsume the other. Skip if the same sharing act for the same item/referent is already recorded; merge/update instead.

payload.name: PreserveExplicitEnumerationsAndThemes
payload.description: When a message explicitly enumerates multiple distinct items (actions, topics, steps, routine segments, coping activities) or explicitly labels a recurring theme, preserve each stated element verbatim with its qualifiers and do not generalize.
content: Scan for explicit enumerations (lists with 'and', commas, or time segments like 'in the morning... in the evenings'); preserve EVERY stated item verbatim with its qualifiers. Do not collapse the list into one broad phrase that drops elements.
If the message attributes separate actions to different participants (e.g., 'for me to X and for them to Y'), record each action under the named participant; never keep only one participant's action.
When the message explicitly labels a recurring theme or pattern, keep the exact label and subject, not a broader category. Do not generalize, paraphrase, or infer elements not stated.
Before committing ADD/MERGE/UPDATE, verify every enumerated element appears in the final stored memory; if any is missing, revise or skip rather than commit a partial memory.

payload.name: DoNotInferUnstatedActivityObjects
payload.description: When a speaker states a duration or activity verb without naming the object/instrument/topic (e.g., 'I've been playing for four months'), do not fill in the object from a question or prior turn; extract only stated facts.
content: If the current message does not explicitly name the object/instrument/topic of an activity, do not take it from an immediate question or from earlier turns. A question's premise is not evidence; the speaker's non-answer does not confirm it.
Extract only what is stated: the speaker, the duration/verb, and any explicit context. If ambiguous, create a candidate with only the stated facts or skip the object entirely rather than guessing.

Do not merge the duration statement with an earlier activity name (e.g., 'learning violin') unless the current message explicitly refers back to the same activity. When in doubt, leave the object out.

payload.name: Preserve attributed and shared statements
payload.description: When a message reports a third-party assessment, a shared or empathized frustration, a desired feeling for others, or echoes another participant's sentiment, retrieve this skill during extraction.
content: For third-party assessments (e.g., 'doctor said...'), extract as a separate candidate with exact wording, evaluator, subject, and person assessed; do not collapse into a generic attitude summary.
For shared or empathized frustrations, extract a relationship/state fact naming both participants and the shared experience verbatim; do not let the speaker's other self-reports subsume it.
For desired-feeling goals, preserve the intended feeling and recipient as its own memory with exact adjectives; do not absorb into a physical description.
For echoed/agreed beliefs, attribute to the current speaker; during CRUD, do not SKIP candidates as duplicates when subjects differ—add or update the correct subject.

payload.name: PreserveGeneralHobbyWithSubtype
payload.description: When a message states a general hobby term (e.g., 'painting') and another message names a specific subtype (e.g., 'watercolor painting'), during extraction store both the general and specific terms without narrowing.
content: If a general category term (e.g., 'mutts', 'painting') is explicitly stated and a specific subtype is also mentioned (e.g., 'Lab mixes', 'watercolor'), store the general term as the category with the subtype as a detail (e.g., 'mutt/mongrel Lab mixes', 'enjoys painting, specifically watercolor'); do not narrow to the subtype alone.
Apply only when the general term appears in the same message or immediately preceding turns; if only a subtype is ever mentioned, store just the subtype and do not infer a general category.
During updates, keep the existing general term and add the subtype as enrichment; do not overwrite the general hobby with the narrower term.

When updating an existing profile with newer subtype details, carry any general descriptor the latest message restates into the new version; do not let the update erase it, unless the new message contradicts or supersedes it.
Preserve the speaker's exact category wording (e.g., 'mutts' vs 'mongrel'); never add a general category that was not stated.

payload.name: Preserve media-activity couplings
payload.description: When a message names a media item (track, album, artist, show, podcast) and ties it to a concrete activity or context (yoga, meditation, commuting), during extraction preserve the item-activity pairing verbatim.
content: For a media item tied to a stated activity, extract the pair verbatim as '<subject> listens to <item> during/for <activity as stated>'; do not reduce to a preference or recommendation.
Apply only when both item and activity are stated in the message; do not infer an activity from a standalone 'I like X' statement or attach an activity not named.
When one turn names multiple items for the same activity, preserve the coupling in each separate candidate; keep exact item names and exact activity wording as stated.

payload.name: Extract explicit focus and priority statements
payload.description: When a message explicitly states that someone is focusing on, prioritizing, or concentrating on something (e.g., 'focusing on studying'), during extraction create a state candidate preserving that stated focus, even if related activities appear.
content: For every explicit focus or priority ('focusing on X', 'prioritizing Y'), record the subject, exact focus wording, and any stated time reference; do not let accompanying concrete activities replace or subsume it.
When one message names multiple distinct focuses, extract one candidate per focus; do not merge them into a single event or activity memory.
Only apply when focusing/prioritizing is explicitly stated; skip messages that only imply importance or describe routine activities, and never guess the focus.
Before creating a new memory, check whether the same focus already exists for that person; if it does, skip it or update only when new details are present.

payload.name: Extract pet/possession ownership states
payload.description: When a message announces acquiring a pet or durable possession or uses a first-person family possessive ('my family's dog'), create an ownership/state memory with the announcement date and exact entity wording.
content: For acquisition announcements, emit a dated ownership state ('<speaker> owns <entity>') alongside any event candidate; skip consumables, borrowed, or hypothetical items and skip if a same-entity ownership state already exists.

For first-person family possessive references (e.g., 'my family's dog', 'my parents' cat'), create a family-pet candidate preserving pet type and possessive wording exactly; do not apply to pets of others or generic mentions.
Never add unstated total counts or merge separate acquisitions; keep each ownership state separate so temporal-count queries remain answerable.

payload.name: Preserve stated effects and naming reasons
payload.description: When a message says a named pet/object helps, cheers, or focuses the speaker, or explains why a person/pet/object was named, extract the stated effect or naming reason verbatim and any past fact it discloses.
content: Emit a preference/state candidate when a named item is subject of benefit ('Tilly helps me stay focused'); quote the benefit verbatim and include only stated categories; skip unnamed or generic statements.

When a speaker explains a name's origin or reason ('named after...', 'I used to have a dog...'), preserve the entity, exact name, and stated rationale; extract any disclosed past fact as a separate candidate.
Do not infer benefits, naming reasons, or categories; skip mentions of a name without an origin/reason, and duplicate only if same fact is already stored (UPDATE/MERGE on new details).

payload.name: Preserve explicit meanings and figurative comparisons
payload.description: When a message states what an object symbolizes or uses a simile/metaphor to characterize a relationship, preserve the exact full stated meaning/figurative wording, not a generic paraphrase. Do not apply to literal statements or unstated meanings.
content: When a message states a named object's meaning ('it stands for...', 'it represents...', 'it's a reminder to...'), preserve EVERY distinct stated component in exact wording; do not collapse multiple meanings into one general paraphrase.

When a speaker uses an explicit simile/metaphor about a relationship or shared endeavor (e.g., 'like having a partner to dance with'), keep the quoted figurative phrase verbatim in the relationship candidate instead of reducing it to 'supportive'.

If the message also states a literal supporting fact, preserve both the literal fact and the exact comparison/meaning; apply only when the comparison is about the relationship or the meaning is about the named object; never infer or complete unstated meanings.

payload.name: Attribute first-person narrated events to the speaker
payload.description: When a chat message narrates an event in first person ('I...', 'we...'), even if it opens by addressing another participant ('Hey Deborah...'), bind the event to the message's speaker. Not for third-person statements or unidentified speakers.
content: When a message narrates an event in first person, set the extracted memory's subject to the message's speaker from metadata, never to the addressee or someone merely greeted. If 'we' is used, keep the group as stated. Do not apply to third-person statements.
If speaker metadata is missing or the first-person referent is ambiguous, SKIP extraction instead of guessing a subject.

When a first-person narration includes a relative time phrase ('last night', 'yesterday'), store the resolved absolute date from the message timestamp AND the original wording. Only when timing is explicitly stated; never invent a date.

When a first-person narration places the speaker in a named place (event, past trip, comparative reply, or exploration), extract the visit/presence fact with person, place, and stated time; preserve exact wording and qualifiers. Do not apply to hypothetical, wish, third-party, or not-yet-visited places; a future scheduled event should be extracted as a future event, never as a past visit. Keep any stated preference/liking for the place as a separate memory; do not merge it into the visit fact or imply the person has visited when only future travel is stated. When the same visit is already recorded, prefer UPDATE/MERGE over duplicate ADD; if no date is stated, leave date unset without inventing one.

When a first-person narration names a location for the speaker's own action, attach the place to the speaker's presence (e.g., 'Tim was in California and had a chat with a fan'), not to a secondary person or object. Do NOT apply when the location modifies another entity ('my friend in California'), the interaction was explicitly remote, or the place is only a future wish. If ambiguous ('a chat with a fan in California'), preserve original wording; do not assert speaker presence or create a travel/location memory. During CRUD, update an existing event memory to include the speaker's presence only if the source message supports it; otherwise leave unchanged.

payload.name: Preserve stated item descriptions and possessions
payload.description: When a message states what a personal possession is, why it is kept, or describes the content of a shown/shared object, extract that factual description.
content: For first-person possession statements with stated purpose/location, extract exact item wording, location, and purpose; do not generalize or apply to items belonging to others. If a preceding clause names the inspiration, keep it verbatim but do not claim the item depicts it unless stated.

When a message answers a question about a shown/shared object's content, record the object and exact stated description; include presenter/recipient relationship if evidenced; otherwise only speaker and description.
Do NOT extract opinions or preferences as descriptions; skip if description already in memory; never invent content, origin, or purpose.

payload.name: Ground extraction to the source message only
payload.description: When extracting a candidate from a message, use only facts explicitly stated in that message, not details from nearby turns.
content: Build each candidate only from facts stated in the message being processed plus speaker/timestamp metadata; import no details from adjacent messages, even if topically related.
When a later message recaps prior facts ('as I mentioned...'), those restated facts may be included; otherwise let later messages create their own candidates or updates.
Do not apply during CRUD/merge, where combining memories across messages is allowed; this governs extraction only.

payload.name: Record non-occurrence of planned activities
payload.description: When a later message explicitly states that a previously planned or intended activity did not happen, or that a previously considered activity has been started/completed, extract the new status and update the earlier plan/consideration memory.
content: Extract a candidate with speaker, activity, exact negation wording, and message date as 'as of' date when non-occurrence is explicit. Do not extract from silence, hypotheticals, or rhetorical questions.

During CRUD, update the earlier plan/interest memory to add non-occurrence status and date while preserving all prior details; if the earlier memory is a distinct dated event, keep it and add a separate state memory.
Do not apply if the activity did occur, if the non-occurrence refers to someone else, or if no earlier plan can be linked.

When a later message states that a previously considered activity has started or been completed (e.g., 'we're going to try now'), extract a candidate for the confirmed action with exact wording and date, and propose an UPDATE to the earlier consideration memory to capture the progression (was considering, then started). Do not delete the original consideration.

payload.name: Preserve geographic attributes of named places
payload.description: When a message names a real place with a stated or widely known geographic attribute (region, multi-state extent, proximity to home), preserve that attribute during extraction without over-applying to vague mentions.
content: When a message states a place is 'close to my home' and identifies it as a named feature (e.g., beach, mountains), extract the proximity relation (e.g., 'Evan has a favorite spot by the beach close to his home').

When a message names a specific real place as the setting of an activity/event/visit, include its unambiguous administrative region (state/province/country) as an attribute; keep the exact place name.

For named landmarks with a widely known multi-state extent (e.g., Smoky Mountains, Grand Canyon), include the recognized states but do not state or imply the person performed separate actions in each state.
Do not add regions or proximity for generic, vague, ambiguous, fictional, or obscure places; never guess a distance, direction, or region.

payload.name: Resolve Generic Entity Labels from Prior Names
payload.description: When a message refers to an entity only via a generic descriptive label (e.g., 'a renowned outdoor gear company') and a previous message or memory names a matching entity, preserve the specific name in extraction only when exactly one match exists.
content: Search earlier conversation and existing memories for a specific entity the same speaker linked to that descriptor or category; if exactly one named entity explicitly matches, record the candidate with that name rather than the generic label.

Do NOT resolve when no specific name exists, when multiple entities could match, when the earlier mention lacks a stated link to the event type, or when the generic label refers to something else; never introduce a name not present in the conversation.

payload.name: Preserve context for short replies
payload.description: When a short reply answers a direct question or references an earlier item/activity, during extraction keep the question's predicate or referent in the candidate, not just the reply's literals.
content: For affirmative replies ('For sure!', 'Definitely!') to a preceding direct question, extract the question's predicate as the subject (e.g., 'Tim enjoys writing about Harry Potter').
For descriptive/exclamatory replies about an item mentioned earlier, link the exact phrase to that item (e.g., 'Audrey describes her new dog beds as super cozy and comfy').
For replies to an activity question that name a different activity, store both the triggering activity and the alternative verbatim, without adding causal links.

payload.name: Carry forward same-session location
payload.description: When a later message in the same session describes an event without a location but an earlier message established one for the same people in a continuing thread, include that location.
content: Check earlier same-session messages for a named location tied to the same subject(s) and a continuing activity thread (e.g., 'traveled to Phuket' then 'we tried scuba diving').
If the earlier location unambiguously frames the current activity, include it explicitly, preserving original activity wording and date; do not repeat if already present.
Do NOT apply when the current activity is unrelated, no earlier location exists, or the link is ambiguous; never guess or add a location from world knowledge.

payload.name: Preserve Completion Events with Timing
payload.description: When a message explicitly states a completed project, activity, milestone, or confirms a specific work instance, extract a standalone event memory and preserve all stated timing and instance details, linking to existing start memories to keep duration reconstructable.
content: Scan for explicit completion/confirmation statements (first-person verbs like finished/completed/watched/read/made/won, or replies like 'Yep!' to a specific project question). Create one standalone event memory per stated fact, keeping exact project type, ordinal, and item name.

Preserve timing qualifiers verbatim and resolve them to calendar intervals when possible; never invent dates/durations. Set world_start/world_end only when the wording ties the event to now (e.g., 'just got the guts'); otherwise leave unset.

When a completion updates an existing start/in-progress memory for the same activity/endeavor, retain the original start date and add the completion date, keeping both wordings. If a milestone matches an earlier start event, store the elapsed duration only when both dates are explicit; never guess ambiguous or missing dates.
Do not apply to vague 'project'/'work' mentions, hypothetical/future/negated statements, third-person activities, or already-recorded facts (UPDATE/MERGE with new details instead of duplicating).

No-inference boundary: never guess a start date unless the duration is an exact whole number of years/months and occurred_at is precise (e.g., 'together for three years' on 25 Feb 2023 → started 2020). Never compute for approximate/hedged durations ('about', 'over', 'just under'), missing dates, or ended states; keep only stated dates.

payload.name: Extract first-person commitments and offers verbatim
payload.description: When a message explicitly states a first-person plan, resolve, offer, or commitment (e.g., 'I won't quit', 'I want to savor the moment', 'I'll mail it'), extract it as a memory, preserving exact wording and any named recipient.
content: Extract explicit first-person commitments/plans/offers (e.g., 'I won't quit', 'I want to savor all the good vibes', 'I can write it down and mail it for you') as a candidate; record speaker, exact action-object wording, and any named addressee. Do not apply to advice, requests, hypotheticals, or third-party statements.
Preserve the object, recipient, and delivery method verbatim; do not paraphrase or import details from other turns (e.g., don't change 'savor all the good vibes' into 'savor the moment with Gina').
If the commitment is directed at a named person or is a service offer for someone, include that recipient; if none is named, do not guess one.
When the same commitment/plan is restated later, submit an UPDATE to the existing memory instead of creating a duplicate.

payload.name: Extract jointly agreed plans with both participants
payload.description: When two named participants explicitly agree to do a shared activity at a stated time (e.g., 'let's paint next Saturday' / 'Sounds good'), extract a single candidate with both participants, the activity, and the exact time.
content: Only when a proposal is met with a clear explicit agreement, extract a joint plan/event candidate naming BOTH participants, the shared activity, and the agreed time exactly as stated; do not compute or guess a calendar date.
Preserve the mutual commitment as one fact; do not split into separate per-subject candidates. Do not apply when only one person expresses interest or when no time is stated.

payload.name: Preserve explicit plan/activity details verbatim
payload.description: When a message plans a visit/meeting/event and explicitly states specific activities, items, venues, or qualifiers (e.g., 'watch a movie', 'fresh pastries', 'snowy landscapes'), preserve every stated detail verbatim in extraction rather than collapsing or dropping. Do not apply when no concrete details are stated.
content: When a speaker explicitly proposes one or more concrete activities for a future meeting (e.g., 'Maybe we can watch a movie or go to the park!'), create a candidate for each proposed activity, attribute it to the speaker, and preserve the exact wording; do not record only the visit/agreement.

When extracting an event/plan candidate, copy each explicitly stated concrete qualifier (scenery, food, venue, named activity) verbatim; do not generalize (e.g., keep 'snowy landscapes', not 'scenic views') and never add inferred details.

When the same plan appears across multiple messages, merge all explicitly stated components (participants, time, venue, activities) into one candidate, keeping every distinct stated detail; if an existing memory is incomplete for the same participants/time, update/merge it instead of creating a duplicate.
Re-check source messages before committing: verify each explicitly stated activity/item/venue appears; skip when messages state no concrete details (only time/place or generic 'meet up').

payload.name: Preserve euphemistic death/loss implications
payload.description: When a message describes a person as no longer alive via euphemistic or indirect phrasing (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him here', 'passed away'), during extraction preserve the exact wording and the implied fact that the person is deceased.
content: Preserve exact euphemistic phrasing when it implies death/permanent absence (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him here', 'passed away', 'I lost him'). Record that the person is no longer alive.
Do not paraphrase away the loss meaning (e.g., write 'a friend who will never be able to support me; I miss him here' rather than 'a friend who will never support her').
Never invent specifics not stated (cause/date of death, exact relationship); keep the speaker's words and certainty.
At CRUD time, add/update the memory to include the death/loss implication whenever it is stated or clearly implied; skip when no loss/death implication exists.

payload.name: Preserve names of deceased from later memorial mentions
payload.description: When a speaker reports a death/loss without naming the person and a later message in the same session names that person in a memorializing context (e.g., 'last photo with X', 'our last one'), update the loss memory with the name and relationship.
content: When a message states a death/loss (e.g., 'I lost a friend', 'she passed away') without naming the person, extract the loss event but keep a placeholder noting the name is not yet stated; never invent a name.

After extracting such a loss, scan subsequent messages for an explicitly named person in a memorializing phrase directly connected to the loss (e.g., 'this is the last photo with <name>', '<name> and I ... it was our last one', 'I miss <name>').
When found, create or update a candidate recording that <name> is the person referenced by the earlier loss, preserving the exact name, the relationship word used, and the original loss wording.
Do NOT apply when the named person appears only in a non-memorial context or the link is ambiguous; never infer a name that is not explicitly stated.

payload.name: ExtractEmbeddedEventAnecdotes
payload.description: When a message explicitly states a past event as an aside in a different-topic message, extract a separate event candidate. Do not apply to hypothetical, planned, or inferred events.
content: Scan every message for explicit past-event phrases like 'Last [weekday] at [place]', 'I went to...', 'at [activity] with [participants]', or concrete past-tense activity mentions, even if the message's main point is a different topic. Create a distinct event candidate for each; do not let the main-topic candidate subsume it.

Resolve relative date references (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday') to an absolute date using the message's own occurred_at timestamp when available. If missing or ambiguous, record the event without a date; never guess or assume a date not derivable from the message.

Preserve the event's exact stated details: subject, activity, participants, and resolved date, keeping original wording where possible. Do not add any participant, location, or date detail that is not stated.

Do NOT apply to hypothetical, future, planned, or inferred events (e.g., 'I would love to go', 'I should go'). Skip extraction when an existing memory already records the same subject's event with the same activity and date.

payload.name: Preserve gaming platforms from setups
payload.description: When a message describes or shows a person's gaming setup, equipment upgrade, or devices/consoles they play on, extract each distinct gaming platform as a standing fact.
content: When a message describes a gaming setup, equipment upgrade, or annotated photo of a setup, create a standing profile/state candidate listing each distinct platform the person uses to play games, separate from any event candidate about the upgrade/purchase.

Preserve platform names exactly as stated or shown (e.g., 'Gamecube', 'PC', 'Playstation'); do not replace with generic labels like 'gaming equipment' or 'setup', and do not list a platform neither named nor shown.
Skip platform extraction when gaming is mentioned only in passing with no device, console, or setup content; never infer platforms not stated or shown.

payload.name: ExtractExplicitPetAttireFacts
payload.description: When a message explicitly mentions an accessory, clothing, or decorative item worn or used by a pet, retrieve this skill during extraction or CRUD to preserve that fact.
content: Identify the pet owner and pet; extract the accessory/attire fact as its own candidate, separate from any activity or event in the message.
Preserve exact item name and stated purpose/reaction (e.g., 'dogs wear hats for fun and treats').
Do not apply when accessory is not explicitly linked to the pet, is hypothetical, joked, denied, or already recorded.
Do not infer colors, quantities, or ownership beyond what the message states; keep original wording.
